name: Lakeflow Jobs (Databricks Workflows)
sku: Lakeflow Jobs as included in the Databricks platform. Documentation reviewed on the AWS docs site. Renamed from Workflows; the record ID is kept because IDs are immutable.

orchestrate.scheduling.note: Jobs run at scheduled times as a core trigger type.

orchestrate.dependency-dag.note: A job is a DAG of tasks with dependencies and conditional execution, with branching and looping supported through a visual editor.

orchestrate.event-triggers.note: A job can start when new data arrives in cloud storage instead of on a clock.

orchestrate.ci-cd.note: Declarative Automation Bundles (formerly Asset Bundles) define jobs and pipelines as source files and deploy them with the Databricks CLI as a single bundle. A separate runner still has to invoke it.

bands.note: Reports run success and logs and metrics for each task, with notifications by email, Slack and webhooks.
A bundle is deployed to a target environment, giving consistent dev, staging and production deployments of jobs and pipelines.

A validation pipeline's task, built with Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines expectations, can gate a downstream task: the pipeline task fails when its expectations fail, so the dependent task never runs. A quality assertion enforced by the job graph itself, not only inside one pipeline.

presentation.tagline: Task-graph orchestration for jobs and pipelines inside Databricks.
